newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end up, but profit taking limits rise.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end up, but profit taking limits rise.

text.p: Stocks closed higher on Wednesday as hopes for government market-boosting steps helped improve the overall sentiment, brokers said.
But most of the day's early gains were erased by profit-taking that emerged as the government remained silent on calls for help, they said.
The composite index ended 1.85 points, or 0.26 percent, higher at a provisional 704.68.
"Selling grew at around the 710-point level as many investors were still pessimistic about an early announcement of boosting measures," said Kim Heung-shik of Hyundai Securities.
Despite the relatively small rise in the index, advancers outpaced decliners by 548 to 343.

The ruling New Korea Party and the Korea Investment Trust Companies' Association asked the government on Tuesday to delay planned sales of stakes in Korea Telecom and other public companies to ease share oversupply fears.
The government has not officially responded to the calls.
"I don't think the improved market sentiment will last for long if the government continues to keep silent. Selling will regain momentum," said a Coryo Securities broker.
The won's sharp drop against the dollar had little immediate impact on the stock market as the downward trend was largely in line with expectations of most investors, brokers said.
The won fell to a new six-year record intra-day low of 843.00 per dollar on Wednesday, shortly before rebounding to 839.50 on dollar selling by the central bank, foreign exchange dealers said.

KorAm Bank rose 600 won to its daily limit of 8,160 on speculation that the bank was the target for acquisition bids by top two conglomerates. The talk was sparked by an increase of Samsung Group's stake in the bank, brokers said.

The exchange said Samsung Group's stake in the bank rose to 17.6 percent from 14.25 percent. Samsung is the bank's second-largest shareholder after Bank of America, which holds 18.55 percent. Daewoo Group comes next with an 11.81 percent stake.

Hwan Yung Steel fell 450 won to its daily limit of 5,260 due to continued concern over the company's financial difficulties. Hwan Yung said it paid back 590 million won of debt on Tuesday, after it failed to settle on Monday. But brokers said the announcement has failed to ease concerns.
